extractions.value: Major criteria: 1. Stiffness in the axial and limb muscles, prominently in the abdominal and thoracolumbar paraspinal muscles leading to a fixed deformity; 2. Superimposed painful spasms precipitated by unexpected noises, emotional stress, or tactile stimuli; 3. Confirmation of continuous motor unit activity in agonist and antagonist muscles by EMG; 4. Absence of any other neurologic disease that could explain stiffness and rigidity. Minor criteria: 1. Presence of anti-GAD antibodies (or antiamphiphysin); 2. Clinical response to diazepam.
extractions.quote: Table 1 Diagnostic criteria for stiff person syndrome [1, 5] ... Although this case did not fulfill the 2 minor criteria, we diagnosed her with SPS based on the major clinical findings and definitive continuous motor activity in the agonist and antagonist muscles on EMG.

extractions.value: Patient had idiopathic chronic kidney disease diagnosed 3 years prior and depression for 15 years, on venlafaxine. Muscle biopsy showed nonspecific focal myositis attributed to sustained muscle contraction rather than autoimmune polymyositis.
extractions.quote: Her medical history revealed idiopathic chronic kidney disease diagnosed 3 years ago and depression for 15 years. ... we concluded that the evidence of nonspecific focal myositis in this patient was not related to immune-mediated response but secondary to sustained muscle contraction.
